news.headline: Is Meta's Next Big Thing Already Here?
news.summary: Meta Platforms (META) stock returned 10.4% over the past month, outperforming the 1.8% return for the S&P 500. Investors have been optimistic about the company following the release of a new app on September 8, 2026. Nearly all of Meta's revenue still comes from ads, but this recent launch may signal the start of a broader business model. So what did Meta launch, and how far has it gotten.

news.headline: Is Reddit Stock a Good Fit For Your Portfolio Risk?
news.summary: Reddit (RDDT) has been listed for only 2.5 years, leaving investors with a short track record to evaluate. Most shareholders likely hold the stock alongside standard index funds that already track broader market movements. So when the market has a good day or a bad one, what does Reddit do to the rest of your money.

news.headline: Why Every Snap Investor Is Looking At This One Number
news.summary: Investors buying Snap (SNAP) stock may be betting on a surprising part of the business: the subscriptions it sells directly to users. Most people still consider Snap an advertising company, but a growing portion of its revenue now comes straight from its audience. The stock lost 28% over the past twelve months, contrasting with a 17.0% return for the S&P 500. So, how many of Snapchat's users actually pay for it.
